topic: VPN error VPN-809 for people returning from leave

notice.title: VPN error VPN-809 for returning staff
notice.body: Some staff returning from leave may see VPN error VPN-809, which means their device certificate has expired. The VPN service itself is working normally. If you are not seeing this error, no action is needed. For those affected: connect to the office network or use the self-service portal to renew your certificate, as expired certificates cannot be renewed over VPN. Certificates are valid for 365 days and must be renewed at least 14 days before expiration. We will update this notice if new information becomes available; check the IT status page for updates.
actions: If seeing VPN-809: connect to office network or use self-service portal to renew certificate
If not affected: no action needed

topic: Print jobs stuck in the queue with error PRN-310

notice.title: Print jobs stuck with error PRN-310
notice.body: Some print jobs are stuck in the queue with error PRN-310, which means the printer is offline or out of paper. If your job is stuck, cancel it and resend when the printer is ready. If the printer is offline or out of paper, there is nothing to do until it is fixed. Check the IT service status page for updates.
actions: Cancel and resend stuck print jobs when the printer is ready.
Check the printer status before sending new jobs.

topic: Wi-Fi sign-in failures with error WIFI-102 after a password change

notice.title: Wi-Fi Sign-In Issue After Password Change
notice.body: Staff who changed their Wi-Fi password may experience sign-in failures with error WIFI-102. The Wi-Fi service is currently operational, and there are no open tickets related to this issue. WIFI-102 occurs when the device's saved Wi-Fi profile no longer matches the network's credentials. For updates, check the IT service status page.
actions: Remove the saved network and join again.
Managed laptops can reinstall the profile from the device management app.

topic: VPN error VPN-809 for people returning from leave

notice.title: VPN Certificate Expiration Issue (Error VPN-809)
notice.body: Some staff returning from leave are encountering VPN error VPN-809, which indicates an expired device certificate. VPN certificates are valid for 365 days and must be renewed at least 14 days before expiration. If your certificate is not expired, no action is needed. For those with expired certificates, renewal cannot be done over the VPN; you must connect to the office network or use the self-service portal to request a new certificate. The SecureLink VPN service is currently operational, and there are no open tickets related to this issue. For updates, check the IT service status page.
actions: If your VPN certificate is expired, connect to the office network or use the self-service portal to request a new certificate.
If your VPN certificate is not expired, no action is needed.
